themes.label: Foreclosure advanced during pending loss mitigation
themes.description: Borrowers allege servicers continued or restarted foreclosure, or otherwise dual-tracked, while loss mitigation, short sale or deed-in-lieu requests were pending or approved.

examples.summary: Consumer claims servicer is delaying loss mitigation review on submitted mortgage assistance application while advancing foreclosure proceedings, and has a history of stalling reviews to push properties into foreclosure sales.
Consumer claims mortgage servicer acknowledged receipt of a complete loss mitigation application but continues to schedule a foreclosure sale before the review process is completed.

Servicer claims to have advanced non-judicial foreclosure proceedings and revoked online account access while loss mitigation requests were still pending, allegedly violating federal servicing standards and RESPA/FDCPA requirements.

themes.label: Flawed application handling and denial explanations
themes.description: Borrowers allege loss mitigation applications were closed prematurely, mishandled, or denied for inconsistent, incorrect or poorly explained reasons without adequate review.

examples.summary: Consumer claims mortgage servicer provided inconsistent reasons for denying payment assistance and failed to properly review multiple loss mitigation options, and requests escalation to FHA/HUD along with comprehensive documentation.

A consumer claims a mortgage servicer closed a modification application before the deadline without notifying the consumer or their attorney, despite allegedly having received the required documents and with time remaining to submit any additional materials.

Consumer claims servicer failed to properly receive and process mortgage assistance application, provided inadequate communication about document deficiencies, repeatedly requested additional documentation with shifting requirements, and ultimately closed the application due to elapsed time despite consumer's documented compliance and timely resubmissions.

themes.label: Modification and trial plan terms or errors
themes.description: Borrowers allege modifications, deferrals or trial plans resulted in higher or miscalculated payments, undisclosed terms, improper cancellation, or processing errors.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a loan modification resulted in an unexplained second principal balance of approximately $29,000 that did not align with modification terms, reducing home sale proceeds and requiring out-of-pocket payment at closing.

Consumer claims the lender offered a loan modification with a higher monthly payment than the original despite the consumer's documented financial hardship and explicit request for more affordable terms.

Consumer claims a hardship mortgage modification resulted in substantially increased monthly payments and an undisclosed balloon payment, allegedly making the borrower's situation worse rather than providing relief.

themes.label: Credit reporting during loss mitigation programs
themes.description: Borrowers allege negative credit reporting or inadequate disclosure of credit effects while enrolled in forbearance, deferral or modification programs.

examples.summary: Mortgage servicer failed to disclose that forbearance payments would be reported to credit bureaus as late or delinquent, resulting in damage to the consumer's credit despite compliance with the agreed repayment program.
Consumer claims the mortgage lender reported missed or late payments to credit bureaus despite instructing the consumer to make no payments during an active loan modification process.

A mortgage servicer reported a borrower's account as 120 days delinquent to credit bureaus despite the borrower being enrolled in approved loss mitigation programs (payment deferral and loan modification) throughout the reporting period, and subsequently refused to correct the inaccurate reporting.

themes.label: Payment handling and servicer communication gaps
themes.description: Borrowers allege servicers refused or blocked payments, failed to respond to inquiries, or communicated poorly or unprofessionally while they tried to manage or resume payments.

examples.summary: Borrower claims mortgage servicer prevented partial payments during forbearance, failed to respond to payment arrangement requests, and was unresponsive to contact attempts regarding post-forbearance options.

Consumer claims the mortgage servicer refuses to assist with verifying a mortgage protection insurance policy except through written fax submission, which the consumer cannot complete due to lack of access to fax equipment.

Consumer claims that after her husband's death, the mortgage servicer rejected her payment, assessed late fees, failed to explain minimum payment requirements for principal reduction, did not respond to written inquiries, and continued sending bills to a deceased person.

brief.headline: Mortgage hardship complaints rising, with claims of foreclosure during pending loss mitigation review
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints in the 'Struggling to pay mortgage' cluster are climbing. The recent three-month average is 900.67 per month against a 752.67 baseline, a velocity of 1.1953 that ranks 6 of 79 clusters. In an AI-reviewed sample of 38 narratives, borrowers claim that loss mitigation applications were mishandled or denied with unclear reasons (33.3%), that foreclosure advanced while loss mitigation was pending (25%), and that modification or trial plan terms were wrong or undisclosed (19.4%). Smaller shares cite payment handling and communication gaps (13.9%) and credit reporting during relief programs (8.3%). These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Mortgage borrowers who are behind on payments and seeking hardship relief such as modifications, deferrals, forbearance or short sales. The AI sample suggests many are vulnerable consumers (65.8%). Complaints are concentrated in CA (13.3%), TX (10.3%) and FL (8.5%). Servicers with elevated lift include Selene Holdings (1.68), LoanCare (1.512), Ocwen (1.389), Carrington (1.372), PennyMac (1.305) and Select Portfolio Servicing (1.257). Larger names such as Rocket Mortgage (0.993) and Shellpoint (0.917) are near or below expected levels for their size.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: weak coordination between loss mitigation review and foreclosure workflows may allow foreclosure steps to proceed while applications are pending. Inconsistent underwriting and denial rationales, application closure and document-tracking errors, and modification or deferral boarding and calculation errors may also contribute. Rising volume across several servicers with above-expected lift points to a sector-wide stress pattern, possibly higher borrower distress combined with servicer capacity or process strain.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Look at the loss mitigation and default servicing function. Check the dual-tracking controls that pause foreclosure referrals and sale steps while an application is pending, application intake and completeness-review timelines and closure rules, denial reason documentation and quality assurance, modification and deferral boarding and payment calculation testing, and credit reporting coding for accounts in relief programs. Also review borrower communication and document access options beyond digital or fax channels.
brief.regulatory_area: Mortgage servicing conduct, particularly loss mitigation handling, foreclosure timing and borrower communication
evidence: Recent monthly average is 900.67 complaints versus a baseline monthly average of 752.67, a velocity of 1.1953.
Monthly complaints rose from 505 in 2025-09 to 937 in 2026-07 and 877 in 2026-08.
Selene Holdings has a lift of 1.68 on 110 complaints, the highest among top companies.
LoanCare has a lift of 1.512 on 99 complaints and Ocwen a lift of 1.389 on 157 complaints.
Rocket Mortgage has the most complaints (330) but a lift of 0.993, and Shellpoint (295) has a lift of 0.917.
33.3% of the 38 sampled narratives involve flawed application handling and denial explanations.
25% of sampled narratives allege foreclosure advanced during pending loss mitigation.
19.4% of sampled narratives involve modification or trial plan terms or errors.
Mean AI-assessed severity is 4.42 out of 5 and 65.8% of the sample involve vulnerable consumers.
0.0% of the 512 recent narratives are templated.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief attributes the rise to several servicers with lift above 1.25 (Selene 1.68, LoanCare 1.512, Ocwen 1.389) and says the largest names, Rocket at 0.993 and Shellpoint at 0.917, are near expected, so it describes a market-wide pattern rather than a size artifact.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: 0.0% of the 512 recent narratives are templated, well under the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top state CA holds only 13.3% of complaints and the top company Rocket holds 330 complaints at a lift of 0.993, so the signal is spread across many states and servicers.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The AI sample has 38 complaints and 512 recent narratives, and the named root cause of foreclosure and loss mitigation coordination is supported by themes covering 25% (foreclosure during review) plus 33.3% (application handling and denials) of the sample.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: The monthly counts rose from 505 in 2025-09 to 888, 937 and 877 in the recent months, so the average of 900.67 does not rest on one peak month and the latest month of 877 is only modestly below the 937 peak after a single dip.

skeptic.note: The brief passes all five checks: the rise is sustained across several servicers, is not templated, is not concentrated in one state or company, and is backed by an adequate sample.

examples.summary: Senior lienholders claim a mortgage servicer and foreclosure trustee refused to distribute foreclosure surplus proceeds and engaged in bad-faith conduct while misrepresenting statutory obligations and ongoing litigation.

Consumer claims mortgage servicer provided inconsistent reasons for denying payment assistance and failed to properly review multiple loss mitigation options, and requests escalation to FHA/HUD along with comprehensive documentation.

Consumer claims a loan modification resulted in an unexplained second principal balance of approximately $29,000 that did not align with modification terms, reducing home sale proceeds and requiring out-of-pocket payment at closing.

Borrower alleges mortgage servicer assessed attorney's fees without active foreclosure on court docket, rejected valid check payments to manufacture delinquency, denied loan modification due to inaccessible digital documents, and initiated foreclosure proceedings in violation of state law.

Servicer allegedly canceled a loan modification without explanation, preventing the borrower from completing trial payments and causing the foreclosure process to begin and property inspection to occur.
